For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] High-quality 3D architectural visualization, one continuous uninterrupted 15.00-second shot with no cuts. The selected target space is the open communal work-and-lounge hall occupying the lower portion of the source image. Treat <Picture 1> as an immutable three-dimensional architectural scene rather than loose design inspiration. Only the camera moves. The red rectangular outline overlaid on the source image is only an annotation marker: it is not part of the scene, and it must never appear in any frame, neither as a line, a glowing edge, a frame border, nor a reflection. Because the source is an open-top axonometric cutaway, the only permitted inferred completions are one plain flat ceiling plane and the vertical extension of the existing walls and partitions upward to meet that ceiling flush.

Preserve exactly the floor plan, room dimensions, wall positions and thicknesses, doors, windows, openings, floor elevations, circulation paths, furniture, fixtures, cabinetry, appliances, sanitary equipment, decorations, materials, colors, textures, lighting direction, and all visible spatial relationships. The principal immutable anchors are: the long central communal work table with four chairs on each of its long sides; the pair of large recliner lounge chairs side by side against the half-height partition on the north side of the hall, with a tall bookshelf at the east end of that partition; the U-shaped bar counter with equipment and two stools on the east side; the long high table with four bar stools on its south side, located between the U-shaped bar and the south wall; the small breakout nook with a round table and three chairs beside the east window wall; the long counter and cabinet run along the west window wall with potted plants; the low credenzas along the south wall with the two booth-style sofa seats near the south-east; and the minimalist white and light-gray material palette with soft daylight entering from the side windows. Nothing may be added, removed, relocated, resized, rotated, recolored, redesigned, duplicated, simplified, or transformed. The only permitted scene additions are the single plain ceiling plane and the upward extension of existing walls and partitions to meet it; no other scene additions are permitted.

From 0.00 to exactly 0.500 seconds, the camera immediately performs a fast, smooth Pedestal Down and Push In from the complete overview toward the central communal work table. The camera simultaneously tilts from the overview angle to a level human-eye direction. The transition occupies no more than the first 0.500 seconds. Do not linger on the aerial view. At exactly 0.500 seconds, the camera optical center is already 1.35 meters above the local finished floor, its pitch is 0 degrees, its roll is 0 degrees, and its optical axis is parallel to the floor. No aerial, elevated, downward-looking, or transitional view is allowed after this point. The horizon remains around 48-52 percent of the frame height. Tabletops, counters, benches, and fixtures show only shallow natural top surfaces and never dominate the frame. Tops of tall cabinets, wall partitions, and door heads are not visible. Never increase the camera height to reveal more of the room.

During the transition, the camera passes only through visible open cutaway volume and is never covered by a wall, ceiling slab, white plane, beam, window frame, cabinet, fixture, appliance, or furniture. Because the source is a roofless cutaway, reconstruct only one continuous flat warm off-white matte ceiling plane at 2.70 meters above the finished floor. Every existing wall and partition of the target space, including the half-height north partition, extends vertically upward in its same material and color until it meets the ceiling plane flush, so that all walls run full height from finished floor to ceiling with no gap, no visible wall-top edge, no exposed cutaway border, and no exterior white void above any wall. The ceiling meets every full-height wall and partition cleanly and remains identical in every frame. Do not create suspended or lowered sections, steps, layers, coffers, coves, light troughs, shadow gaps, decorative panels, curved forms, skylights, exposed beams, tracks, linear HVAC slots, pendants, chandeliers, or newly invented light layouts. Preserve the original daylight and lighting direction, and ensure the completed ceiling never crosses or blocks the lens during the descent.

From exactly 0.500 to 15.000 seconds, use the entire remaining 14.50 seconds to perform one complete 360-degree clockwise architectural orbit around the central communal work table. The route is a true rounded-rectangle closed path following the visible clearance ring around the central table: the south lane between the table and the low credenzas along the south wall, the west lane between the table and the window-wall counter, the narrow north lane between the table and the pair of recliners, and the east lane between the table and the long high table with bar stools. The camera physically travels through four distinct sides of the target space while continuously looking inward toward the central communal work table. Do not interpret the orbit as a fixed-position pan, short arc, partial semicircle, repeated lateral slide, or simple rotation from one position.

Maintain an average angular travel rate of approximately 24.83 degrees per second. Completing the full 360-degree circuit and returning to the starting camera coordinate takes priority over slow motion, lingering compositions, pauses, or long easing.

From 0.500 to 4.125 seconds, complete the first 90 degrees, traveling from the south side beside the low credenzas along the south wall, looking north across the central work table toward the two recliners and the partition, to the west side in the lane between the window-wall counter and the table, looking east across the table toward the U-shaped bar, along the visible collision-free route. At exactly 4.125 seconds, the camera is at the first-quarter viewpoint.

From 4.125 to 7.750 seconds, complete the second 90 degrees, traveling from the west window-wall lane to the north side, in the narrow gap between the central work table and the pair of recliners, looking south across the table toward the south credenzas and booth seats. At exactly 7.750 seconds, the camera is opposite its human-eye starting position and has completed 180 degrees.

From 7.750 to 11.375 seconds, complete the third 90 degrees, traveling from the north recliner lane to the east side, in the lane between the central work table and the long high table with bar stools, looking west across the table toward the west window wall. At exactly 11.375 seconds, the camera has completed 270 degrees.

From 11.375 to 15.000 seconds, complete the fourth and final 90 degrees, traveling from the east high-table lane back to the south side beside the low credenzas. At exactly 15.000 seconds, the camera has completed a true total angle of 360 degrees and returns to the same physical position, 1.35-meter optical-center height, pitch, roll, yaw, focal length, target point, horizon, and composition established at 0.500 seconds.

Use a constant 24 mm architectural lens, level horizon, straight verticals, deep focus, restrained motion blur, and no fisheye distortion. After 0.500 seconds, the optical center remains locked exactly 1.35 meters above the local finished floor. It may not rise, descend, bob, or crane. Only horizontal yaw changes are permitted while following the closed path.

If the camera falls behind a required angular checkpoint, smoothly increase its travel and angular speed to reach the checkpoint on time. Never sacrifice the final 360-degree closure for a slow view. Maintain strict geometric and temporal consistency: no layout reconstruction, object movement, morphing, disappearance, duplication, newly invented decoration, new openings, new rooms, material changes, people, text, logos, watermarks, or any red outline or annotation graphics. No cuts, teleportation, direction reversal, camera-height drift, wall penetration, furniture collision, ceiling penetration, lens obstruction, unstable verticals, or excessive motion blur.

overall_soundscape: Very quiet indoor room tone with soft, steady ventilation ambience. No voices, footsteps, impacts, or prominent environmental sounds.
